subject: POC: readiness cadence, keys, and peering — sprint plan
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@therapico.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Tran <jason.tran@therapico.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — initial MAP items

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the low-latency responses on the health-data templates. Procurement asked me to pull together the actionable items so we can lock timelines internally. Quick ask: can you confirm what you need from our side to get the POC environment live (org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, and VPC peering)? We have a tight window: approval meeting on 5/22 and we want the POC to start the week of 5/29 if possible.

I've attached a one-page summary of our evaluation priorities. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Director, Platform Integrations
Therapico

Attachment: therapico_evals_priorities.pdf (summary)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@therapico.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — initial MAP items

Emma — great to hear. I've sketched a compact MAP focused on the items you listed so we can line up internal approvals and the POC start. High level:

- Redwood deliverables (pre-POC): generate tenant in our control plane, pre-provision dedicated API key set for the trial org, prepare temporary ingress IP range for allowlist testing, and prepare VPC peering runbook.
- Customer deliverables (pre-POC): confirm CIDR/IP ranges for allowlist and peering, approve SOC/IP security questionnaire answers, and provide the contacts who will accept the peering request.

Attached is a short spreadsheet that maps owners and target dates. Proposed timeline (subject to your internal approval):
- 5/11: org created + API keys issued (sandbox keys)
- 5/12–5/17: network allowlist testing and handshake (temporary IPs)
- 5/18–5/22: VPC peering prep and DocuSign (if required by procurement)
- 5/29: POC run starts (3 weeks)

Questions for you now:
1) Can you share the IP ranges (or a firewalled jump host) we should allow?
2) Who should we send the peering request to (name + email + cloud account id)?
3) Any procurement constraints about static credentials vs. ephemeral keys?

I'll loop in Monica and Aditya for the technical steps — they'll send the runbook and peering checklist.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners/dates)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@therapico.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — initial MAP items (technical runbook)

Hi Emma / Marcus — quick technical note from the infra side. I'm attaching a concise peering + allowlist checklist that we've used successfully on similar healthcare POCs. Key items below to unblock us quickly:

- API Keys / Org setup:
  - We can create a trial org in our control plane. Please confirm the desired org name and primary admin email.
  - We will issue two API key pairs: one sandbox key (no prod data) and one monitor key for usage metrics. Keys can be rotated; we support short-lived tokens if your security team prefers.

- IP allowlist / temporary testing:
  - If you can provide a single jump-host IP for initial tests, we can open only that source for the first 48–72 hours.
  - For broader allowlist: provide the CIDR blocks for both your testing subnet and any CI runners that will call the API.

- VPC peering steps (high-level):
  1) Share your cloud account id + VPC id + preferred region.
  2) We'll create a peering request from our side and include the peering config in the runbook.
  3) You accept the peering and add routes for the peered CIDR.
  4) We validate connectivity and remove the temporary jump-host rule after baseline tests.

Action items for Emma / Therapico (suggested owners):
- Provide: CIDR/IP ranges, cloud account id, peering contact (name + email) — due 5/15
- Confirm whether procurement requires an SOW/DocuSign for peering — due 5/16

I'll attach the VPC peering runbook (PDF) and an editable spreadsheet mapping owners. If you prefer a call, I have availability 5/13 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: vpc_peering_instructions.pdf (runbook), network_handshake_template.txt (stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@therapico.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — final readiness check and go/no-go cadence

Emma — thanks for the quick responses in the doc. We're tracking the MAP in the attached workbook and have penciled in the sprint dates. Short status update and a single blocking question:

Status (as of 5/15):
- Org created in control plane: done (redwood-therapico-trial)
- Sandbox API keys: issued and shared via secure token service (I emailed the admin token to the address you provided)
- Temporary jump-host allowlist: waiting on your IP; we can keep it open for 72 hours for validation
- VPC peering: pending your cloud account id + peering contact to accept the request

Blocking question: procurement asked if we can support a short SOW (one page) that references the peering handshake and data handling rules. We can provide a template; would that speed approval on your side?

If we get the IP + peering contact by EOD 5/15 and procurement sign-off on a short SOW by 5/18, we are green to start the POC on 5/29 as requested. Otherwise we should plan a one-week slip.

Happy to run a 15-minute alignment call today to close outstanding items.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer — Infra | Redwood Inference

Inline references: HubSpot deal THX-4821, MAP doc: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/therapico/poc-specs
